verdict.rationale: Factory documents droid exec as a headless one-shot mode "ideal for ... batch processing", and says it can put code review, QA, and documentation on autopilot across repos. That points to multi-item automation. However, bulk work appears to rely on scripting droid exec in loops or on persistent automations; no native bulk-select or apply-to-many-items operation is documented. Missing for 10: a documented first-party bulk operation across many items (e.g. multi-select issues, sessions, or repos), stated limits or concurrency for batch runs, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: `droid exec` runs as a one-shot command that completes a task and exits, making it ideal for CI/CD pipelines, shell scripts, and batch processing.
Put code review, QA, and documentation on autopilot across your repos.
repository coverage, stage health, and persistent automations
